docs.title: Welcome!
docs.text:
AKMenu-Next is a menu for your DS, DSi or 3DS that lets you browse your SD card and launch games and homebrew through nds-bootstrap or Pico-Loader. It takes the classic Acekard/Wood menu (via akmenu4) and builds a lot on top of it: modern loaders, DSiWare, game covers, theme music, plugins, per-game settings and loads more. Its upgraded theme system adds covers, music, custom icons and extra top-screen options, and your favourite Acekard and Wood themes still work too!

Some of the things it can do:

  • Run DS games with nds-bootstrap or Pico-Loader, with per-game settings
  • Cheats from a usrcheat.dat database
  • DSiWare on a DSi/3DS SD card or a DSpico
  • Themes, game covers and theme music
  • Plugins for opening other file types (emulators, video players and so on)
  • Favourites, Recently Played, multiple save slots and more

docs.title: Which version do I need?
docs.text:
There's a separate download for each kind of setup. Grab the one that matches what you're running it on:

You have... Install guide Loader A DS flashcart (R4, Acekard, DSTT, etc.) Flashcart Edition Pico-Loader or nds-bootstrap A DSpico DSpico Edition Pico-Loader (nds-bootstrap optional) A modded DSi, running from the console's own SD card DSi Edition nds-bootstrap A modded 3DS/2DS, running from the console's own SD card 3DS Edition nds-bootstrap

If you're using a flashcart in a DSi or 3DS, you still want the flashcart (or DSpico) version. The DSi and 3DS versions are only for running off the console's own SD card slot.

docs.title: Installing AKMenu-Next
docs.text:
Info

AKMenu-Next is an enhanced, actively developed take on the Acekard/Wood menu (forked from akmenu4) that runs Nintendo DS software & homebrew through nds-bootstrap & Pico-Loader. It adds DSiWare support, cheats, plugins, per-game settings and an upgraded theme system with game covers and music, while still supporting Acekard/Wood themes. For in-game controls such as soft-reset, see the nds-bootstrap controls page.

Pick the tab for your setup below. Not sure which one you need? There's a table on the home page.

Before you start

  • You'll need 7-Zip (or any extractor that handles .zip and .7z).
  • Use a decent, genuine SD card. A lot of "corrupted files" and "theme missing" problems turn out to be fake or dying cards, so if your card is new it's worth testing it first.
  • All the paths in this guide are from the root of your SD card, i.e. the top level, not inside another folder.

This needs a modded Nintendo DSi. If yours isn't modded yet, follow dsi.cfw.guide first.

docs.title: Installing AKMenu-Next Flashcart Edition
docs.text:
1. Download the latest release of AKMenu-Next Flashcart Edition.

  2. Extract the downloaded akmenu-next-flashcart.zip file with 7-Zip.

  3. Copy the following files/folders to the root of your SD card:

    • _nds folder
    • _pico folder
    • BOOT.NDS

    Already using TWiLight Menu++ or another menu?

    If there's already a BOOT.NDS on your SD card that something else relies on, rename the AKMenu-Next one (e.g. akmenu-next.nds) before copying it over, then launch it from your kernel.

docs.title: Installing a game loader
docs.text:
AKMenu-Next doesn't run DS games by itself, it hands them off to a loader. You need at least one of these. You can install both and switch between them whenever you like, even per game.

  • Pico-Loader only supports certain flashcarts, but if yours is on the list it's a good choice.
  • nds-bootstrap works on pretty much any flashcart that can run homebrew. The Flashcart Edition uses nds-bootstrap by default.
Pico-Loadernds-bootstrap

Warning

Using the wrong version of Pico-Loader could damage your flashcart! If you are unsure which version to use, check the Supported Platforms section. If your flashcart isn't listed, use nds-bootstrap instead.

  1. Download the latest release of Pico-Loader. Pick the zip that matches your flashcart, using the Supported Platforms table to work out which one that is.

  2. Extract the downloaded Pico_Loader_YOUR_FLASHCART_HERE.zip file with 7-Zip.

  3. Copy the contents of the zip into the _pico folder on your SD card (create it if it isn't there). When you're done, you should have _pico/picoLoader7.bin and _pico/picoLoader9.bin.

  4. Boot AKMenu-Next, press START and go to Settings. In the Game loader settings tab, change Game Loader to Pico-Loader, then press A and confirm to save.

  1. Download the latest release of nds-bootstrap.

  2. Extract the downloaded nds-bootstrap.zip file with 7-Zip.

  3. Copy the contents of the zip into the _nds folder on your SD card. You should end up with files like _nds/nds-bootstrap-release.nds and _nds/nds-bootstrap-hb-release.nds.

  4. That's it, nds-bootstrap is already the default loader on the Flashcart Edition. If you've previously switched to Pico-Loader, press START, go to Settings > Game loader settings and set Game Loader back to nds-bootstrap.

Note

The first time you launch a game with nds-bootstrap you'll get a message about first-time setup. It creates a large pagefile.sys in _nds, which can take a minute. This only happens once.

You can now launch BOOT.NDS from your flashcart's kernel, or set up autobooting below so you go straight into AKMenu-Next.

docs.title: Autobooting AKMenu-Next
docs.text:
Note

If you can't find your flashcart in the Autoboot folder (check Autoboot/README.txt too, as a lot of clones share files), skip this section and just launch BOOT.NDS from your kernel. On some kernels you can make a copy of BOOT.NDS called default.nds to have it chainload automatically.

  1. Open the Autoboot folder in the AKMenu-Next files and find the folder that matches your flashcart.

  2. Copy the contents of that folder (not the folder itself) to the root of your SD card. Overwrite anything it asks about.

  3. If your flashcart is a DSTTi clone that needs extra boot files, look in the Supplementary DSTTi Clone Files folder. The YSMenu compatibility list can tell you which file your cart wants. If it isn't there, make copies of TTMenu.dat from the DSTT & DSTTi folder and rename them to whatever your cart needs.

Slot-1 carts that need DLDI patching

Most kernels DLDI patch homebrew for you. A few, like the Games n' Music, or Slot-2 carts booted into NDS mode, might not. If AKMenu-Next can't see your SD card, DLDI patch BOOT.NDS with your cart's driver first.

docs.title: Autobooting AKMenu-Next
docs.text:
Note

Autobooting AKMenu-Next on a DSi needs Unlaunch or Astronaut installed.

Unlaunch UsersAstronaut Users

  1. Turn on your DSi while holding A and B.

  2. In the Unlaunch menu, go to OPTIONS.

  3. Set NO BUTTON (or a button of your choice) to the akmenu-next entry. The bottom screen should show akmenu-next.dsi when it's selected.

  4. Turn your DSi off and back on. It'll now boot straight into AKMenu-Next.

  1. Turn on your DSi while holding A and B.

  2. In the Astronaut menu, go to Settings, then Change Boot Options.

  3. Select default boot option and choose Launch something from SD.

  4. Find akmenu-next.dsi on the SD card and select it.

  5. Press go back at the bottom, then Save on the previous screen.

  6. Turn your DSi off and back on. It'll now boot straight into AKMenu-Next.

1. Download the latest release of AKMenu-Next 3DS Edition.

  2. Extract the downloaded akmenu-next-3ds.zip file with 7-Zip.

    Warning

    If you use TWiLight Menu++ on your 3DS and want to keep it, don't copy over BOOT.NDS, as it'll overwrite the one TWiLight Menu++ uses. You don't need it anyway since you'll be launching AKMenu-Next from the home menu.

  3. Copy the following files/folders to the root of your SD card:

    • BOOT.NDS (read the warning above)
    • akmenu-next.cia

  4. Download the latest release of nds-bootstrap.

  5. Extract the downloaded nds-bootstrap.zip file with 7-Zip.

  6. Copy the contents of the zip into the _nds folder on your SD card.

  7. Put the SD card back in your 3DS and turn it on. Open FBI, go to SD, find akmenu-next.cia, select it and choose Install CIA.

  8. Launch akmenu-next from the 3DS home menu.

Tip

If AKMenu-Next doesn't show up on the home menu after installing (or you're updating an older version), restart your 3DS.

Once it's installed you can delete akmenu-next.cia from your SD card if you want the space back.

docs.text: AKMenu-Next can launch DSiWare from your 3DS's SD card through nds-bootstrap. See Running DSiWare.

docs.title: First boot
docs.text:
The first time AKMenu-Next starts, it'll ask you to pick a language. Choose one and it'll restart into the menu. You can change it later in the System settings tab of the settings menu.

After that you'll see the top level of the file browser. What's listed depends on your setup:

Setup What you'll see Flashcart in a DS / DS Lite microSD Card, Favourites, Recently Played, Slot 2 Card Flashcart or DSpico in a DSi / 3DS microSD Card, DSi SD (if a card is in the console), Favourites, Recently Played, Slot 2 Card DSi / 3DS SD card DSi SD, Favourites, Recently Played, Slot 1 Card

Head into your SD card, find a game and press A. Have a look at Using the Menu for everything else.

docs.title: What your SD card should look like
docs.text:
Here's roughly what you'll have once everything is installed. You don't need to match it exactly, but if something isn't working it's a handy thing to compare against:

SD:/
├── _nds/
│   ├── akmenunext/            <- AKMenu-Next's own files
│   │   ├── cheats/usrcheat.dat
│   │   ├── language/
│   │   ├── plugins/
│   │   ├── ui/                <- themes go in here
│   │   ├── globalsettings.ini <- created on first boot
│   │   └── launcher.nds
│   ├── nds-bootstrap-release.nds
│   ├── nds-bootstrap-hb-release.nds
│   └── nds-bootstrap-nightly.nds (optional)
├── _pico/                     <- flashcart & DSpico only
│   ├── picoLoader7.bin
│   └── picoLoader9.bin
├── BOOT.NDS
└── (your games, in whatever folders you like)

Info

Need help or want to chat about AKMenu-Next? Check out the AKMenu-Next GBAtemp thread.

docs.title: Running DSiWare
docs.text:
AKMenu-Next can run DSiWare in two ways, depending on your setup:

Setup Works? How Modded DSi, running AKMenu-Next from the console's SD card Yes nds-bootstrap, Unlaunch or Astronaut Modded 3DS, running AKMenu-Next from the console's SD card Yes nds-bootstrap DSpico in a DSi or 3DS Yes Pico-Loader Any flashcart (including DSpico) in a DS or DS Lite No The DS and DS Lite don't have the hardware to run DSi software Other flashcarts in a DSi or 3DS No Most flashcarts run in DS mode only. If your console is modded, put your DSiWare on the console's SD card instead

DSiWare dumps need to end in .nds, .dsi, .srl or .ids for AKMenu-Next to pick them up. If yours has no extension at all, or is called something like 00000000.app, just rename it to something like Flipnote Studio.nds.

docs.title: DSi and 3DS SD card
docs.text:
This is for the DSi and 3DS editions of AKMenu-Next, running from the SD card inside the console.

  1. Make sure nds-bootstrap is installed in the _nds folder on your SD card (the install guide covers this).

  2. Copy your DSiWare onto the SD card. You can put it in any folder you like, a DSiWare folder on the root keeps things tidy.

  3. Launch it from AKMenu-Next like any other game.

That's all there is to it on a 3DS.

docs.title: Using Unlaunch or Astronaut to boot DSiWare (DSi only)
docs.text:
On a DSi with Unlaunch installed, you can have AKMenu-Next hand DSiWare over to Unlaunch instead of nds-bootstrap. This runs the title more like it would from the system menu, so it's worth a try if something doesn't work properly through nds-bootstrap.

Got Astronaut instead? That works exactly the same way, since Astronaut supports launching DSiWare just like Unlaunch does. Everything below applies to both. The option is still called Unlaunch in the settings, so just pick that.

  • To use Unlaunch for all DSiWare, go to Settings > Game loader settings and set DSiWare booter to Unlaunch.
  • To use it for one title, highlight it, press Y, then Y again for its settings, and change DSiWare booter there.

AKMenu-Next quietly falls back to nds-bootstrap if Unlaunch can't be used: if neither Unlaunch nor Astronaut is installed, if the title is 64MB or bigger, or if you're on a 3DS (which can't run either of them).

docs.title: Saves
docs.text:
DSiWare doesn't use .sav files. Instead, each title can have a public save (.pub) and/or a private save (.prv). AKMenu-Next reads the sizes from the title itself and creates blank ones the first time you play, so you don't need to make them yourself.

Where they go:

  • nds-bootstrap uses saves sitting right next to the ROM (e.g. DSiWare/Flipnote.pub) if they're already there. If not, they go wherever your normal save settings say, so with Use 'saves' folder turned on that's DSiWare/saves/Flipnote.pub.
  • Unlaunch / Astronaut always needs the saves right next to the ROM. If they're in a saves folder, AKMenu-Next moves them next to the ROM for you before booting.

If you already have saves from TWiLight Menu++ or a NAND dump, rename them to match the ROM's name and put them next to it, e.g. Flipnote.nds, Flipnote.pub, Flipnote.prv.

docs.title: DSpico
docs.text:
Console compatibility

This only works with your DSpico plugged into a DSi or 3DS. It won't work on an original DS or DS Lite, as those don't have the DSi hardware needed for DSi-mode software.

To run DSiWare (and encrypted DS ROMs), Pico-Loader needs some files dumped from your console first. You only need to do this once.

  1. Download the DSpico BIOS and NAND dumper utility.

  2. Put pico_file_dump.nds on the root of your DSpico's SD card.

  3. Make a DSiWare folder on the root of the SD card, and put any DSiWare you'd like to play inside.

  4. Put the SD card back in your DSpico and boot into it.

  5. Find pico_file_dump.nds in the menu and launch it. It'll start dumping straight away.

  6. Once it says it's finished, press the power button to turn the console off.

  7. Boot into AKMenu-Next and make sure Game Loader in Settings > Game loader settings is set to Pico-Loader.

  8. That's it! Head into your DSiWare folder and launch something.

Note

If your DSi/3DS is modded and has an SD card in it, you'll also see a DSi SD entry at the top level of AKMenu-Next. DSiWare launched from there goes through nds-bootstrap (installed on the console's SD card), not Pico-Loader. That's what the DSi and 3DS SD card section above is about.

docs.title: Optional: tidying up your SD card
docs.text:
The dumper copies quite a few NAND folders onto your SD card. They need to stay there, but if you don't want to see them in the file list you can mark them as hidden. AKMenu-Next doesn't show hidden files unless you turn on Show hidden files in the settings.

Folders and files worth hiding:

  • _pico folder
  • photo folder
  • shared1 folder
  • shared2 folder
  • sys folder
  • _picoboot.nds
  • boot.nds

Since the BIOS and NAND files have already been dumped, you can also delete pico_file_dump.nds now.

WindowsmacOSLinux

  1. Open the SD card in File Explorer.

  2. Hold Ctrl and click each of the files and folders you want to hide.

  3. Right click one of the selected items and choose Properties.

  4. Under Attributes, tick Hidden, then press OK.

  5. If it asks, choose "Apply changes to the selected items, subfolders, and files", then press OK.

  6. They'll disappear from File Explorer, that's normal. You can see them again by turning on "Show hidden files" in File Explorer's "Folder Options".

  1. Open Terminal and go to your SD card. Replace SDCARD with your card's name as it appears in Finder:

    cd /Volumes/SDCARD

  2. Hide the files and folders:

    chflags hidden _pico photo shared1 shared2 sys _picoboot.nds boot.nds

To unhide something later, run the same command with nohidden instead of hidden.

You'll need the fatattr tool (it's in most distros' repos, e.g. sudo apt install fatattr). Then, from the root of your mounted SD card:

fatattr +h _pico photo shared1 shared2 sys _picoboot.nds boot.nds

Use -h instead of +h to unhide them again.

Put the SD card back in your DSpico and boot into the menu. The hidden stuff won't show up any more, but DSiWare will still work.

Tip

Files and folders starting with a . are hidden in AKMenu-Next too, so the ._ files macOS likes to leave everywhere won't clutter up your list.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text: Some questions that come up a lot. If something's actually broken, the Troubleshooting page might be more help.

docs.title: How do I soft-reset or quit back to the menu?
docs.text: With nds-bootstrap, press L + Down + SELECT in game. You can change this combo with Settings > System settings > Menu Hotkey, or set your own. More in-game controls are on the nds-bootstrap controls page.

docs.title: Should I use Pico-Loader or nds-bootstrap?
docs.text:
If you're on a flashcart that Pico-Loader supports, or a DSpico, give Pico-Loader a go. It's also the only option for .ndz files. If your cart isn't supported by Pico-Loader, use nds-bootstrap. On a DSi or 3DS SD card it's nds-bootstrap only.

You don't have to pick just one. Install both and you can switch loaders for an individual game in its per-game settings, which is handy if one game works better with the other loader.

docs.title: What flashcarts does this work with?
docs.text:
Pretty much any flashcart that can run homebrew, either through its own kernel or using one of the autoboot files that come with AKMenu-Next. If you're not autobooting, some carts (like the Games n' Music, or some Slot-2 carts booted into NDS mode) might need BOOT.NDS DLDI patched first.

Pico-Loader only works on certain flashcarts, but nds-bootstrap will work on anything that runs homebrew.

docs.title: Can I run DSiWare on AKMenu-Next?
docs.text:
Yes, on these setups:

  • A modded DSi or 3DS running AKMenu-Next from the console's SD card
  • A DSpico plugged into a DSi or 3DS

Normal flashcarts can't run DSiWare since they run in DS mode, and the DS and DS Lite don't have the hardware for it at all. See Running DSiWare for how to set it up.

docs.title: Can I use this alongside TWiLight Menu++?
docs.text:
Yep. The main thing is not to overwrite the BOOT.NDS that TWiLight Menu++ uses.

  • DSi: skip copying BOOT.NDS and launch akmenu-next.dsi from Unlaunch or TWiLight Menu++ instead.
  • 3DS: skip copying BOOT.NDS. You launch AKMenu-Next from the home menu anyway.
  • Flashcart: rename AKMenu-Next's BOOT.NDS to something else (like akmenu-next.nds) and launch it from your kernel or from TWiLight.

Both menus use nds-bootstrap from the same _nds folder, so you only need it installed once. Both can use a saves folder next to your ROMs too, so your saves should carry across as long as the Save extension and Use 'saves' folder settings match how TWiLight has them.

docs.title: How can I use a nightly build of nds-bootstrap?
docs.text: Put nds-bootstrap-nightly.nds in your _nds folder (next to nds-bootstrap-release.nds), then go to Settings > Game loader settings and set nds-bootstrap version to nightly. You can also just use nightly for one game, from its per-game settings. There's more detail on the updating page.

docs.title: What games are compatible?
docs.text:
Most retail games should work with the latest nds-bootstrap or Pico-Loader. ROM hacks, translations and randomisers might be hit or miss.

AKMenu-Next just hands the game to the loader, so game compatibility problems should be reported to the loader instead:

  • nds-bootstrap issue tracker
  • Pico-Loader issue tracker

Homebrew works too. On a DSi or 3DS, some homebrew only runs properly from a flashcart. If something doesn't load, try setting Homebrew Loader to nds-bootstrap-hb in Settings > Game loader settings.

docs.title: Where are my saves?
docs.text: By default (Flashcart, DSi and 3DS editions) they're in a saves folder next to the ROM, e.g. Games/saves/Mario.sav. The DSpico edition puts them right next to the ROM, e.g. Games/Mario.sav. You can change both of these, see Saves.

docs.title: Can I have more than one save for a game?
docs.text: Yes, every game has four save slots. Press Y on a game, Y again for its settings, and change Choose Save Slot in the Features tab. See Save slots.

docs.title: Can I play GBA games?
docs.text:
On a DS or DS Lite with an EZ-Flash 3-in-1 (or compatible) expansion pack, yes, .gba files from your SD card can be loaded onto it. You can also boot a real GBA cart (or Slot-2 flashcart) from the Slot 2 Card entry.

On a DSi or 3DS there's no GBA slot, but you can set up a GBA emulator (like GBARunner3) as a plugin so .gba files open in it.

docs.title: Can I use my old Acekard / Wood themes?
docs.text: Yes! Drop them into _nds/akmenunext/ui/ and pick them from START > Themes. See Themes.

docs.title: Can I change the language?
docs.text:
Go to Settings > System settings > Language. Right now AKMenu-Next comes with English, French, German, Italian, Spanish, Russian, Japanese, and Simplified and Traditional Chinese. If you'd like to help translate, the language files are in the AKMenu-Next repo.

The Language Override setting in Game loader settings is something different: it changes which language games start in, not the menu.

docs.title: I have a question not listed here
docs.text: Ask it in the AKMenu-Next GBAtemp thread. If you want to report a bug or request a feature, please open an issue on the AKMenu-Next issue tracker.

docs.title: Plugins
docs.text:
Plugins let AKMenu-Next open file types it doesn't understand on its own. A plugin just tells AKMenu-Next "when someone opens a .gbc file, start this emulator and pass it the file". It's how you get things like Game Boy, NES or SNES ROMs, or videos, showing up in your file list and launching with one press of A.

Installing PluginsMaking Plugins

  1. Go to the AKMenu-Next Plugins page and download the plugin(s) you want.

  2. Extract the download on your computer.

  3. Inside you should find an _nds folder (and maybe some other files or folders next to it). Copy all of it to the root of your SD card.

    • On Windows, if it asks about replacing files, choose Replace the file in the destination.
    • On macOS, choose Merge, not Replace. Replace will wipe your existing _nds folder, AKMenu-Next and all.

  4. Put the SD card back and start AKMenu-Next. Files with the plugin's extension will now show up in the file browser and can be launched like anything else.

Note

Plugins are loaded when AKMenu-Next starts up, so if you add one while the menu's running, restart it before the new files show up.

GBA files and the EZ-Flash 3-in-1

If you've got a gba plugin installed and an EZ-Flash 3-in-1 in Slot-2, .gba files will go to the 3-in-1 instead of the plugin. Take the 3-in-1 out if you want to use the plugin.

docs.title: The plugin INI
docs.text:
Each plugin is a single .ini file in _nds/akmenunext/plugins/. The file name is the extension it handles, so gbc.ini handles .gbc files, nes.ini handles .nes files and so on. Extensions aren't case sensitive.

Here's what one looks like:

[plugin]
path=app/myemulator.nds
argv=1
bootstrap=0
hbargv=0

And here's every key you can use:

Key Default What it does path (none) The .nds file to launch. This is the fallback if dsipath/ntrpath aren't set. dsipath (none) Use this .nds instead when AKMenu-Next is running in DSi mode (DSi/3DS SD card, or a DSpico in a DSi/3DS). ntrpath (none) Use this .nds instead when AKMenu-Next is running in DS mode (flashcarts, or anything on a DS/DS Lite). argv 0 Set to 1 to pass the selected file's path to the emulator. Almost every emulator needs this. bootstrap 0 Set to 1 to launch the plugin through nds-bootstrap-hb. This only kicks in on a DSi/3DS SD card, it's ignored on flashcarts. hbargv 0 Set to 1 to also pass the file through nds-bootstrap-hb's HOMEBREW_ARG setting. Only used when the plugin is actually going through nds-bootstrap-hb. extension file name Override the extension, if you want the INI to be called something different from the extension it handles.

You need at least one of path, dsipath or ntrpath, otherwise the plugin is skipped. If you set dsipath but no path, the plugin only works in DSi mode (and the same the other way round with ntrpath). You'll get an error if you try to open the file in the other mode.

dsipath and ntrpath are handy for emulators that have separate DS and DSi builds, or if one version just runs better on one kind of setup.

Warning

Don't put // comments on the end of lines like you might see in some examples. Everything after the = is read as the value, so argv=1 // passes the file won't do what you want. If you want notes in your INI, put them on their own line starting with ; or //.

docs.title: Where paths point to
docs.text:
Paths in a plugin INI can be written a few ways:

Written as Points to app/emu.nds Relative to the plugins folder, so _nds/akmenunext/plugins/app/emu.nds _nds/emu.nds From the root of the SD card /apps/emu.nds From the root of the SD card fat:/apps/emu.nds or sd:/apps/emu.nds That exact drive and path

The usual place to keep the emulator itself is _nds/akmenunext/plugins/app/, which is what the official plugins do. That way your path can just be app/emu.nds.

docs.title: How plugins are launched
docs.text:
Plugins are treated as homebrew, so they follow your Homebrew Loader setting (in Settings > Game loader settings):

  • AKMenu-Next (the default): the emulator is booted directly.
  • nds-bootstrap-hb: the emulator is booted through nds-bootstrap-hb.
  • Pico-Loader: the emulator is booted through Pico-Loader.

The one exception is bootstrap=1. On a DSi or 3DS SD card, that forces nds-bootstrap-hb for that plugin no matter what your Homebrew Loader is set to. This is for emulators that were really made for flashcarts and only work properly from the DSi SD through nds-bootstrap-hb.

If you'd rather your own Homebrew Loader setting always wins, turn on Override plugin defaults in Other Settings.

docs.title: Plugin icons
docs.text:
To give your file type an icon, put a standard Nintendo DS banner file in _nds/akmenunext/plugins/icons/, named after the extension, e.g. gbc.bin for .gbc files. If there isn't one, the files get the default "unknown file" icon.

Banner files are the same format as the banner inside a .nds file. You can pull one out of an existing .nds with tools like ndstool (ndstool -x game.nds -t banner.bin).

docs.title: Per-file banners
docs.text:
Want a specific file to have its own icon? Put a DS banner file in the same folder as it, named the file's full name with .bin on the end:

Pokemon Crystal.gbc
Pokemon Crystal.gbc.bin   <- icon for that one file
Mario.nds
Mario.nds.bin             <- replaces Mario's built-in icon

A per-file banner wins over everything else: the ROM's own icon, and the plugin's extension icon. It works for any file the browser is showing, so as long as the file type is covered by a plugin (or you're showing all files), it'll use it.

docs.title: Example: a Game Boy plugin
docs.text:
Say you've got a Game Boy emulator called gbemu.nds that accepts a ROM path through argv, and you want .gb and .gbc files to open in it.

  1. Put gbemu.nds in _nds/akmenunext/plugins/app/.

  2. Make _nds/akmenunext/plugins/gb.ini:

    [plugin]
path=app/gbemu.nds
argv=1

  3. Make a copy of it called gbc.ini (each extension needs its own INI).

  4. Optionally, add gb.bin and gbc.bin icons to _nds/akmenunext/plugins/icons/.

  5. Restart AKMenu-Next and your Game Boy ROMs will show up.

If you make something you think other people would like, consider sharing it on the GBAtemp thread!

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Open the settings with START > Settings, or press L + Y from the file browser.

Getting around the settings menu:

  • L / R switch between tabs
  • Up / Down pick an option
  • Left / Right change it
  • A saves (it'll ask you to confirm)
  • B backs out without saving anything

Some options only show up on certain setups. For example, Game Loader only appears on flashcarts and the DSpico, since the DSi and 3DS versions only use nds-bootstrap. If you can't see something listed here, that's probably why.

All of these get saved to _nds/akmenunext/globalsettings.ini.

docs.title: System settings
docs.text: Option Choices What it does Language Any installed language Press A on it to choose the menu language. AKMenu-Next restarts to apply it. Menu Hotkey L-↓-SELECT, L-R-START, L-R-SELECT, L-R-A-B-↓, L-R-B-Y-↓, L-R-A-B-X-Y, Custom The button combo nds-bootstrap uses to soft-reset back to AKMenu-Next while you're in a game. See custom hotkeys below. Slot-2 mode ask, gba, nds What happens when you open Slot 2 Card. ask gives you a choice each time.

docs.title: Custom hotkey
docs.text:
If none of the preset combos suit you, set Menu Hotkey to Custom and put your own combo in _nds/akmenunext/ndsbs.ini:

[ndsbs]
hotkey=284

The value is a hex number made by adding together the buttons you want:

Button Value Button Value A 1 Right 10 B 2 Left 20 SELECT 4 Up 40 START 8 Down 80 R 100 X 400 L 200 Y 800

So L + Down + SELECT is 200 + 80 + 4 = 284. Remember it's hex, so L + R + START is 200 + 100 + 8 = 308. If hotkey= is left empty, nds-bootstrap just uses its own default.

Warning

Don't delete ndsbs.ini, even if you never use a custom hotkey. nds-bootstrap won't launch without it and you'll get an "INI error" message.

docs.title: Interface settings
docs.text: Option Choices What it does Filelist style Old school, Modern, Internal, Small Icons How the file list looks. You can also cycle through these with SELECT. See file list styles. Scrolling speed Fast, Medium, Slow How fast the list scrolls when you hold a direction. Icon source Theme Icons, Global Icons, Built-in icons Where folder, save and other file icons come from. Theme Icons uses the theme's own icons folder first, then falls back to _nds/akmenunext/icons. Global Icons skips the theme and uses _nds/akmenunext/icons. Built-in icons ignores both. Animation on, off Animated game icons and other little bits of motion. 12-hour clock on, off Show the clock as 11:45 PM instead of 23:45. Game covers on, off Show box art on the top screen, if your theme supports it. See game covers. Theme music on, off Play the theme's background music, if it has any.

docs.title: File system settings
docs.text:
Option Choices What it does Set file list type NDS, NDS + SAV, ALL Which files show up in the browser. NDS shows games, GBA ROMs and anything you have a plugin for. NDS + SAV adds save files. ALL shows everything. Show hidden files on, off Show files and folders that have the hidden attribute set. Save extension .nds.sav, .sav Whether saves are named Game.sav or Game.nds.sav. Use 'saves' folder yes, no Put saves in a saves folder next to the ROM instead of right beside it. Sort by Name, Game Title, Date Asc, Date Desc How files are ordered in each folder.

Have a look at Saves for a table of where save files end up with each combination.

Warning

Changing Save extension or Use 'saves' folder doesn't move your existing saves. If you change either of them, move your save files to match, or your games will start from a fresh save.

docs.title: Game loader settings
docs.text:
Option Choices What it does Game Loader nds-bootstrap, Pico-Loader Which loader runs your DS games. Flashcart & DSpico only. nds-bootstrap version release, nightly Which nds-bootstrap build to use. Nightly needs _nds/nds-bootstrap-nightly.nds. DS-Only Mode on, off Run games in DS mode, even on a DSi or 3DS. Can help with games that misbehave in DSi mode. TWL CPU Speed on, off Run DS games at the DSi's faster CPU speed. Can reduce lag in some games, but break others. DSi & 3DS only. Card Read DMA Auto, on, off nds-bootstrap's card read DMA. Leave it on Auto unless you've been told a specific game needs it changed. Language Override System, Japanese, English, French, German, Italian, Spanish, Chinese, Korean Make games start in a different language than your console is set to. Only works for games that actually include that language. DS Phat Colors on, off Mimic the slightly different colours of the original DS screen. DSi mode only. DSiWare booter nds-bootstrap, Unlaunch What to launch DSiWare with on a DSi. Unlaunch also works if you have Astronaut installed instead. See Running DSiWare. DSi mode only. Homebrew Loader AKMenu-Next, nds-bootstrap-hb, Pico-Loader What to launch homebrew with. See below.

Most of these settings are only for nds-bootstrap. If you're using Pico-Loader they won't make a difference.

docs.title: Homebrew Loader
docs.text:
• AKMenu-Next (the default) boots homebrew directly. This is what you want most of the time.
  • nds-bootstrap-hb runs homebrew through nds-bootstrap's homebrew build. Useful on a DSi or 3DS SD card for homebrew that was only ever meant to run from a flashcart and won't work otherwise. Needs _nds/nds-bootstrap-hb-release.nds.
  • Pico-Loader runs homebrew through Pico-Loader instead. Needs Pico-Loader in _pico.

docs.title: Other Settings
docs.text: Option Choices What it does Ignore CRC16 Errors on, off Some ROM hacks and translations have a broken checksum on their icon, so they show a generic icon. Turn this on to show the icon anyway. Cheat in Game(AR) on, off The global switch for cheats. Games can override this in their per-game settings. Save Slot Override off, 0, 1, 2, 3 Force every game onto the same save slot. 0 is the default slot. Autorun Last ROM on, off Launch the last game you played as soon as AKMenu-Next starts. Hold B while booting to skip it. Override plugin defaults on, off Always use your Homebrew Loader setting for plugins, even if the plugin asks for nds-bootstrap-hb. See Plugins.

docs.title: Resetting your settings
docs.text:
If you've got yourself into a mess, you can put everything back to default:

  1. Delete _nds/akmenunext/globalsettings.ini.
  2. Copy _nds/akmenunext/globalsettings-init.ini from a fresh download of AKMenu-Next (the same edition you're using) into _nds/akmenunext on your SD card.
  3. Boot AKMenu-Next. It'll pick up the fresh settings and ask you for your language again.

If you skip step 2 it still works, but you'll get AKMenu-Next's built-in defaults rather than the ones tuned for your edition.

There are a few other files in _nds/akmenunext you can delete to reset other things:

File What it holds favorites.ini Your favourites recent.ini Recently Played lastsave.ini The last game you played (used by autorun and to remember your folder) gamedata.bin Per-game settings and save types backlight.ini Screen brightness

docs.title: Themes
docs.text:
AKMenu-Next has an upgraded theme system. On top of everything classic themes could do, AKMenu-Next themes can have game covers, background music, their own file icons, and extra top-screen bits like the date and your DS username.

It can use three kinds of themes:

  • AKMenu-Next themes, with all the extras above
  • Acekard / AKAIO themes
  • Wood R4 themes

Acekard and Wood themes work as they are, and you can add the new features to them yourself (see Creating Themes).

A few themes come with AKMenu-Next already (Blue Skies, Starlight and DSpico, each with a "Game Covers" version), and there are loads more online.

Installing ThemesCreating Themes

Use AKTheme Studio to create custom themes for AKMenu-Next.

If you want to edit the theme files by hand, start by copying one of the bundled themes and changing things bit by bit.

docs.title: Installing a theme
docs.text:
1. Download a theme:
    • For themes made for AKMenu-Next, have a look at the AKMenu-Next theme repository.
    • For older Acekard/AKAIO/Wood R4 themes, try the Wood R4/AKMenu theme repository.
  2. Open the .7z archive with an extractor such as 7-Zip.
  3. Copy the theme's folder from the archive into _nds/akmenunext/ui/ on your SD card.
  4. Put the SD card back in your flashcart or console and start AKMenu-Next.
  5. Press START and choose Themes.
  6. Highlight the theme you just installed and press A to pick it, then press X (OK).
  7. Say Yes when it asks to restart, and AKMenu-Next will reload with your new theme.

docs.title: The theme picker
docs.text:
Themes are split into two groups: Standard Themes and Game Cover Themes (the ones that can show box art, see game covers below). Press Right on a group to open it and Left to close it. B backs out without changing anything.

Check the folder path

The theme's folder has to sit directly inside _nds/akmenunext/ui. For example, a theme called HatsuneMiku should end up like this:

_nds/akmenunext/ui/HatsuneMiku/uisettings.ini

A really common mistake is ending up with it nested one level too deep, like _nds/akmenunext/ui/HatsuneMiku/HatsuneMiku/, which happens when the archive has a folder inside a folder. A theme like that won't show up in the picker at all. Move the inner folder up a level and it'll appear.

If a theme is broken

If the theme you're using goes missing or turns out to be broken, AKMenu-Next will tell you and switch to another valid theme (Blue Skies if it can) so you're not left with a menu that won't boot. If you've got no valid themes at all, you'll get a message telling you to add one to _nds/akmenunext/ui.

docs.title: Game covers
docs.text:
If you're using a theme that supports covers, AKMenu-Next can show a picture of the box art on the top screen when you highlight a game. The bundled "Game Covers" themes all support this.

You'll need to get the cover images yourself and put them on your SD card. Covers are .bmp files, named either after the game's 4-letter game code or the ROM's file name. AKMenu-Next looks in these places, in this order:

DS games (.nds, .ndz, .dsi, .srl, .ids)

  1. _nds/covers_code/ using the game code, e.g. _nds/covers_code/ASME.bmp
  2. _nds/covers_name/ using the file name, e.g. _nds/covers_name/Super Mario 64 DS.bmp
  3. _pico/covers/nds/ using the game code (where Pico-Launcher keeps its covers)

GBA games (.gba)

  1. _nds/covers_code/, then _nds/covers_name/, then _pico/covers/gba/, trying both the game code and the file name in each.

The file name is the ROM's name without its extension, so Super Mario 64 DS.nds looks for Super Mario 64 DS.bmp. You can find a game's code by pressing Y on it in AKMenu-Next.

If you already have covers set up for Pico-Launcher, AKMenu-Next will just use them, no need to copy anything.

Cover image tips

  • Any normal uncompressed .bmp works (16, 24 or 32-bit, or paletted). 32-bit BMPs can have transparency.
  • Keep them small. Anything bigger than 256×192 gets cropped, and files over 1MB or 1024 pixels in either direction are skipped.
  • Some covers (including a lot from Pico-Cover) have a strip of black or transparent padding on the right. If there are 4 or more empty columns on the right edge, AKMenu-Next trims them off for you.

You can turn covers off with Settings > Interface settings > Game covers.

docs.title: Theme music
docs.text: Some themes come with background music. You can turn it off with Settings > Interface settings > Theme music.

docs.title: What's in a theme
docs.text:
A theme is just a folder inside _nds/akmenunext/ui/. The folder name is the theme name that shows up in the picker. At minimum it needs a uisettings.ini with a [global settings] section, plus its images.

Here's what a full theme folder looks like:

MyTheme/
├── uisettings.ini      <- colours, positions, and features (required)
├── custom.ini          <- extra top-screen bits like username and date (optional)
├── upper_screen.bmp    <- top screen background (256×192)
├── lower_screen.bmp    <- bottom screen background (256×192)
├── title_left.bmp      ┐
├── title_bg.bmp        ├ window title bars
├── title_right.bmp     ┘
├── btn2.bmp, btn3.bmp, btn4.bmp   <- buttons of different widths
├── spin_btn_left.bmp, spin_btn_right.bmp
├── brightness.bmp      <- brightness button
├── folder_up.bmp       <- folder up button
├── menu_bg.bmp         <- start menu background
├── card_icon_blue.bmp  <- little SD activity icon (max 32×32)
├── progress_wnd.bmp, progress_bar.bmp
├── calendar/
│   ├── clock_numbers.bmp, clock_colon.bmp
│   ├── day_numbers.bmp, year_numbers.bmp
│   └── date_numbers.bmp (optional, see the date section below)
├── icons/              <- optional theme-specific file icons
└── bgm.wav / bgm.bcstm <- optional music

The two screen backgrounds have to be exactly 256×192, and nothing can be bigger than the screen (number strips can be up to 10 screens tall).

docs.title: Image format
docs.text:
All theme images must be 16-bit BMPs in X1 R5 G5 B5 format (also called RGB 5:5:5). That's what the DS draws natively. In GIMP, when you export as BMP, open the advanced options and choose 16 bit (X1 R5 G5 B5).

Pure black (#000000) pixels are treated as transparent. If you actually want black, use a very dark grey like #080808 instead.

docs.title: Theme icons
docs.text:
Put DS banner .bin files in your theme's icons/ folder to give it its own folder, save, favourites (and so on) icons. They use the same file names as the ones in _nds/akmenunext/icons/, so copy that folder into your theme and edit from there. Any icon your theme doesn't include falls back to the global one.

Players can ignore theme icons with Settings > Interface settings > Icon source.

docs.title: Config files
docs.text:
uisettings.ini controls the interface: colours, where things go, how big they are, and whether features like covers are switched on. custom.ini is optional and adds extra things to the top screen, like the DS username, the date, your own text, or a picture.

Both are normal INI files: a section name in square brackets, then key = value lines under it. Positions and sizes are in pixels. Anything you leave out just uses the built-in default.

A setting only applies to the section it's in, so x and y under [big clock] move the clock, while x and y under [date] move the date. Most sections also have show = 1 (visible) or show = 0 (hidden).

Here's a chunk of Blue Skies' uisettings.ini as an example:

[global settings]
formBodyColor = 0x5e06
formTextColor = 0x7fff
spinBoxNormalColor = 0x7fff
spinBoxTextColor = 0x4d80
spinBoxFrameColor = 0x35ad

[main list]
textColor = 0x2d6b
selectionBarColor1 = 0x20e2
selectionBarColor2 = 0x1482
selectionBarOpacity = 100

[big clock]
x = 6
y = 94
show = 1

docs.title: Colours
docs.text:
Colours are written as DS 15-bit values in hex. Each of red, green and blue goes from 0 to 31, and they're packed together like this:

colour = red + (green × 32) + (blue × 1024)

A few to get you going:

Colour Value White 0x7fff Black 0x0000 Red 0x001f Green 0x03e0 Blue 0x7c00 Mid grey 0x4210

If you've got a normal 0–255 colour from an image editor, divide each channel by 8 (and round down) to get the 0–31 value.

docs.title: Scroll indicators
docs.text:
These keys in [global settings] colour the little scroll arrows and bars you see in the settings, theme list, Help and About windows:

Key Controls spinBoxNormalColor The arrow for a direction you can't scroll any further in spinBoxTextColor The arrow for a direction you can scroll in, plus the scrollbar thumb spinBoxFrameColor The outline of the scrollbar 
[global settings]
spinBoxNormalColor = 0x001f
spinBoxTextColor = 0x7fff
spinBoxFrameColor = 0x4210

docs.title: Clock and calendar
docs.text:
These all go in uisettings.ini:

Section Keys What it is [big clock] x, y, show The big clock, drawn using calendar/clock_numbers.bmp [am pm] x, y, color, show AM/PM label, only shown when the 12-hour clock is on [calendar year] x, y, show The year [calendar month] x, y, show The month [calendar dayx] x, y, show A small day number [calendar day] x, y, dw, dh, highlightColor, show The month grid. dw/dh are the size of each day cell

If your design doesn't have room for the calendar, set the show values to 0 and use a [date] in custom.ini instead.

docs.title: Extra top-screen bits (custom.ini)
docs.text: Everything in custom.ini is drawn on top of upper_screen.bmp.

docs.title: Username
docs.text:
Shows the name from the console's system settings:

[user name]
x = 60
y = 173
color = 0x7fff
show = 1

docs.title: Your own text and picture
docs.text:
[custom text] takes text, x, y, w, h, color and show.

[custom picture] takes file, x, y and show. file is the full path to the BMP from the root of the SD card, e.g. /_nds/akmenunext/ui/MyTheme/avatar.bmp. It has to be a small image, the file can't be bigger than 10KB (roughly 64×64).

docs.title: Date and time
docs.text:
[date] shows the current date, and the time if you want it. With font = 0 it uses normal text, so you don't need any extra graphics:

[date]
x = 8
y = 148
color = 0x7fff
show = 1
format = DD/MM/YYYY
showTime = 1
font = 0

The format can be:

Value Example DD/MM/YYYY 09/11/2026 MM/DD/YYYY 11/09/2026 YYYY/MM/DD 2026/11/09

showTime = 0 hides the time. Otherwise it follows the player's 12-hour clock setting, so it shows either 23:45 or 11:45 PM.

docs.title: Using your own digits
docs.text:
Set font = 1 to draw the date with your own number graphics from calendar/date_numbers.bmp instead:

  • The image must be 9 pixels wide and 140 pixels tall: ten 9×14 digits stacked on top of each other, 0 at the top down to 9 at the bottom.
  • The slashes aren't drawn. Instead there's a 9 pixel gap between each part, so you can put slashes (or dots, or whatever you like) into your background image.
  • format still decides the order of day, month and year.
  • The time isn't shown in this mode, even with showTime = 1.

docs.title: Supporting game covers
docs.text:
To make your theme show covers, add a [cover] section to its uisettings.ini. Themes without one never show covers, and they'll be listed under Standard Themes instead of Game Cover Themes.

[cover]
x = 140
y = 44
darken = 0
fade = 0
Key What it does x, y Where the cover's top left corner goes. Leave one out to centre the cover on that axis. darken Darken the whole top screen behind the cover, from 0 (normal) to 100 (black). Nice for making covers pop on a busy background. fade Make the cover see-through, from 0 (solid) to 100 (invisible).

Most people make two versions of their theme, one with covers and one without, since covers usually need space on the top screen that the calendar would otherwise use.

docs.title: Theme music
docs.text:
Put music files straight in the theme folder, next to the images. AKMenu-Next looks for:

  • bgm.bcstm and bgm1.bcstm up to bgm9.bcstm
  • bgm.wav and bgm1.wav up to bgm9.wav

So that's up to 20 songs per theme. Each time the music starts, one is picked at random and looped. If a file can't be played, it's skipped and another one is picked.

docs.title: BCSTM (recommended)
docs.text:
BCSTM is the 3DS music format, and it's the better choice: the files are much smaller than WAV, and it supports loop points, so a song can have an intro that plays once and then loop the rest.

  • DSP-ADPCM, mono or stereo, up to 48,000 Hz. 32,000 Hz is a good choice, since the DS outputs at about 32.7 kHz anyway, so going higher just wastes space.
  • Loop points saved in the file are used.
  • Wii U .bfstm files won't work.
  • Tools like VGAudio, LoopingAudioConverter or μ-wave (which runs in your browser) can make them.

docs.title: WAV
docs.text:
• Uncompressed RIFF/WAVE PCM, 16-bit signed, mono or stereo. 22,050 Hz mono keeps the size down.
  • Always loops from the very start.

  • Audacity or FFmpeg can export this. For example, with FFmpeg:

    ffmpeg -i song.mp3 -ac 1 -ar 22050 -c:a pcm_s16le bgm.wav

Note

If you're sharing your theme, please only include music you're allowed to share, and credit it (the bundled themes include a Music Attribution.txt for this). AI-generated art and music aren't accepted for themes submitted to the AKMenu-Next repo.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Something not working? Have a look through the errors below. If yours isn't here, the FAQ might help, or you can ask in the GBAtemp thread.

Check the About screen first

Press START and choose About. It tells you which version of AKMenu-Next you're on, whether it thinks it's running from a flashcart, DSpico or SD card, and which versions of nds-bootstrap and Pico-Loader it can find. If a loader says N/A, AKMenu-Next can't see it, which explains a lot of problems on its own.

docs.title: "AKMenu-Next system files are missing or corrupted"
docs.text:
AKMenu-Next couldn't find its own files. It needs at least _nds/akmenunext/ and _nds/akmenunext/launcher.nds on the root of your SD card.

  • Make sure you copied the whole _nds folder from the download, and that it's on the root of the card, not inside another folder.
  • If it was working before, your SD card might be on its way out. Back up your saves and test your SD card with H2testw or F3. Fake and failing cards are honestly the most common cause of this.
  • Then reinstall AKMenu-Next from the install guide.

docs.title: "AKMenu-Next cannot launch: no valid themes are installed"
docs.text:
There aren't any themes AKMenu-Next can use in _nds/akmenunext/ui.

  • Check there's at least one theme folder in there, with a uisettings.ini file directly inside it (not in another folder inside it, see the themes page).
  • If you deleted the bundled themes, copy them back from the download.
  • If your themes are definitely there, the files might be corrupted. Same as above, test your SD card.

docs.title: "The selected theme is missing or corrupt"
docs.text: The theme you had picked is broken or gone, so AKMenu-Next switched to another one. You can carry on using the menu as normal. If you want your old theme back, reinstall it and pick it again from START > Themes.

docs.title: White screen, black screen, or it freezes on boot
docs.text:
• If you're on a flashcart, make sure your kernel is actually able to launch homebrew, and try launching BOOT.NDS from the kernel menu instead of autobooting.
  • If AKMenu-Next can't see your SD card, BOOT.NDS might need to be DLDI patched for your cart.
  • If you have Autorun Last ROM turned on, the problem might be the game, not the menu. Hold B while AKMenu-Next starts to skip autorun.
  • Try a different theme by editing uiName in _nds/akmenunext/globalsettings.ini to Blue Skies.

docs.title: "Loader not found"
docs.text:
AKMenu-Next can't find the files for the loader it's trying to use. The message tells you which file it was looking for.

Loader It needs nds-bootstrap _nds/nds-bootstrap-release.nds nds-bootstrap (nightly) _nds/nds-bootstrap-nightly.nds nds-bootstrap-hb (homebrew & plugins) _nds/nds-bootstrap-hb-release.nds Pico-Loader _pico/picoLoader7.bin and _pico/picoLoader9.bin

Either install the missing loader (see the install guide), or switch to one you do have in Settings > Game loader settings. Don't forget to check the game's own per-game settings too, it might be set to a different loader or to nightly.

If it's a plugin file you're launching, the missing file might be the emulator itself. Check the path in the plugin's INI.

docs.title: "INI error: ndsbs.ini is missing from _nds/akmenunext or is corrupt"
docs.text: AKMenu-Next needs _nds/akmenunext/ndsbs.ini to launch nds-bootstrap. Copy it back over from a fresh download of AKMenu-Next (it's called ndsbs-init.ini in the download, which works fine, AKMenu-Next will rename it on the next boot).

docs.title: "There is not enough space on the disk"
docs.text:
AKMenu-Next couldn't create the save file for the game. Saves can be up to a few MB (and some games, like WarioWare D.I.Y., need 32MB), so make sure you've got a decent amount of free space. Keeping at least 50MB free is a good idea, as nds-bootstrap and Pico-Loader need some room for their own files too.

If you've got loads of free space and still see this, the SD card might be read-only, corrupted, or failing. Run a disk check on it and test the card.

docs.title: It shows "Initializing nds-bootstrap" and then a message about first-time setup
docs.text: That's normal! The first time you use nds-bootstrap it has to create a big file (_nds/pagefile.sys). Just press OK and wait, it only happens once.

docs.title: "DSiWare launch requires a ROM on the DSi SD card and DSi mode"
docs.text: You tried to launch DSiWare through nds-bootstrap from somewhere that doesn't support it. Through nds-bootstrap, DSiWare has to be on the console's SD card (the DSi SD entry). If you're on a DSpico, either set the game to use Pico-Loader, or move it to the console's SD card. See Running DSiWare.

docs.title: "Could not create the DSiWare save files on the SD card"
docs.text: Same as the "not enough space" error above, but for DSiWare's .pub/.prv saves. Check your free space and that the card isn't read-only.

docs.title: "An error occurred", "Data abort", "Failed to load arm9" or similar
docs.text:
Errors like these come from the game loader, not AKMenu-Next. A few things worth trying first:

  • Update your loader to the latest version (see Updating).
  • Try the other loader, if you have both. You can do this for just that one game.
  • If you're on nds-bootstrap, try turning DS-Only Mode or TWL CPU Speed on or off for that game.
  • Turn cheats off for that game.
  • Make sure the ROM itself isn't a bad dump.

If none of that helps, report it to the loader you're using:

  • nds-bootstrap issue tracker
  • Pico-Loader issue tracker

Getting a log from nds-bootstrap

If you create an empty file called debug.txt in your _nds folder, AKMenu-Next turns on nds-bootstrap's logging and debug mode. This can be really helpful to attach to a bug report. Delete the file again when you're done, as it slows things down.

docs.title: My game started with a blank save / my save is gone
docs.text: AKMenu-Next looks for saves based on your Save extension and Use 'saves' folder settings. If they don't match where your saves actually are, it'll make a new blank save instead. Check where saves go, move your save to the right place, and make sure the game's save slot is set to default (and that Save Slot Override is off).

docs.title: My game doesn't save properly
docs.text: Try setting the save type manually. Press Y on the game, then Y again, and change Select a save type. If you're not sure what it should be, look the game up in a save type list, or ask in the GBAtemp thread.

docs.title: Cheats aren't showing up
docs.text:
• Make sure usrcheat.dat is at _nds/akmenunext/cheats/usrcheat.dat. If AKMenu-Next can't find it, the Cheats button won't show at all.
  • If the button's there but nothing comes up, your database doesn't have that game (or that version of it). Try a newer database.
  • Cheats aren't available for homebrew.

docs.title: Cheats aren't working in game
docs.text:
• Make sure Cheat in Game(AR) is on, either globally in Other Settings or in the game's per-game settings.
  • Make sure you saved your cheat selection with X.
  • If you're using Pico-Loader, update it. Older versions don't support cheats.

docs.title: My ROM hack or translation has a blank/generic icon
docs.text: Its banner checksum is probably wrong. Turn on Ignore CRC16 Errors in Other Settings and the proper icon should show.

docs.title: A file type I have a plugin for doesn't show up
docs.text:
• Make sure the INI is directly in _nds/akmenunext/plugins/ and named after the extension (e.g. gbc.ini).
  • Restart AKMenu-Next, plugins are only loaded at startup.
  • Check the INI has at least a path (or dsipath/ntrpath), otherwise it's ignored.
  • Check your Set file list type isn't doing anything odd, or press L + SELECT to show all files.

docs.title: Game covers aren't showing
docs.text:
• Make sure you're using a theme that supports covers (it'll be listed under "Game Cover Themes").
  • Check Game covers is turned on in Interface settings.
  • Check the cover's name and location, see game covers. Press Y on the game to double check its game code.
  • Make sure the cover is a normal BMP and not too big.

docs.title: No theme music
docs.text:
• Not every theme has music.
  • Check Theme music is turned on in Interface settings.
  • If it's your own theme, check the format of your music files, see theme music.

docs.title: Can't see the DSi SD card on my DSpico
docs.text: The DSi SD entry only shows up when the DSpico is running in DSi mode on a DSi or 3DS, and there's an SD card in the console itself.

docs.title: Updating AKMenu-Next
docs.text:
AKMenu-Next, nds-bootstrap and Pico-Loader are all separate projects, so they're updated separately too. You don't have to update them all at once.

You can check what you've currently got by pressing START and choosing About. It shows your AKMenu-Next version and the versions of any loaders it can find.

The latest versions and changelogs are here:

  • AKMenu-Next releases
  • nds-bootstrap releases
  • Pico-Loader releases

Mac users: Merge, don't Replace

When macOS asks what to do with an existing folder, always pick Merge. Replace deletes the whole old folder first, which takes your themes, plugins, cheats and settings with it.

Your settings are safe

Updating won't reset your settings, favourites or recently played list. AKMenu-Next ships its defaults as -init.ini files and only uses them if you don't already have a real one, so overwriting is fine.

docs.title: Updating AKMenu-Next
docs.text:
FlashcartDSpicoNintendo DSiNintendo 3DS

  1. Download the latest release of AKMenu-Next Flashcart Edition.

  2. Extract the downloaded akmenu-next-flashcart.zip file with 7-Zip.

  3. Copy the following files/folders to the root of your SD card:

    • _nds folder
    • BOOT.NDS (or whatever you renamed it to)

  4. Overwrite the existing files when asked.

You don't need to copy the _pico folder or the autoboot files again, those don't change between AKMenu-Next versions.

  1. Download the latest release of AKMenu-Next DSpico Edition.

  2. Extract the downloaded akmenu-next-pico.zip file with 7-Zip.

  3. Copy the following files/folders to the root of your SD card:

    • _nds folder
    • BOOT.NDS
    • _picoboot.nds (only if you autoboot AKMenu-Next)

  4. Overwrite the existing files when asked.

  1. Download the latest release of AKMenu-Next DSi Edition.

  2. Extract the downloaded akmenu-next-dsi.zip file with 7-Zip.

  3. Copy the following files/folders to the root of your SD card:

    • _nds folder
    • akmenu-next.dsi
    • BOOT.NDS (skip this if you use TWiLight Menu++)
    • title folder (only if you have AKMenu-Next installed as a HiyaCFW app)

  4. Overwrite the existing files when asked.

  1. Download the latest release of AKMenu-Next 3DS Edition.

  2. Extract the downloaded akmenu-next-3ds.zip file with 7-Zip.

  3. Copy the following files/folders to the root of your SD card:

    • _nds folder
    • akmenu-next.cia
    • BOOT.NDS (skip this if you use TWiLight Menu++)

  4. Overwrite the existing files when asked.

  5. Install akmenu-next.cia with FBI again. You might need to restart your 3DS before the new version shows up.

docs.title: Updating nds-bootstrap
docs.text:
1. Download the latest release of nds-bootstrap.

  2. Extract the downloaded nds-bootstrap.zip file with 7-Zip.

  3. Copy the contents of the zip into the _nds folder on your SD card, overwriting the old files.

Using nightlies

Want to try a nightly build? These come straight from nds-bootstrap's GitHub Actions now:

  1. Go to the nds-bootstrap Actions page and click the newest successful run.
  2. Scroll down to Artifacts and download build. You'll need to be signed in to GitHub for the download to show up.
  3. Extract the zip, then extract the nds-bootstrap.7z inside it with 7-Zip.
  4. Copy nds-bootstrap-nightly.nds into your _nds folder, next to the release version.

Then set nds-bootstrap version to nightly in Settings > Game loader settings. You can keep both and flip between them, or just use the nightly for one game from its per-game settings.

docs.title: Updating Pico-Loader
docs.text:
1. Download the latest release of Pico-Loader. Pick the one that matches your flashcart, same as when you installed it. If you're not sure, check the Supported Platforms table. DSpico users want Pico_Loader_DSPICO.zip.

  2. Extract the downloaded zip with 7-Zip.

  3. Copy the contents of the zip into the _pico folder on your SD card, overwriting the old files.

docs.title: Using the Menu
docs.text: This page goes over the day-to-day stuff: getting around, launching things, saves, cheats and so on. For a rundown of every option in the settings menu, see Settings.

docs.title: File browser
docs.text:
Button What it does D-Pad Up/Down Move through the list D-Pad Left/Right Jump up/down a page A Open a folder or launch the selected file B Go back to the parent folder L (tap) Also goes back to the parent folder X Jump to Favourites Y File info for the selected file (this is where per-game settings live) START Open the start menu SELECT Cycle through file list styles R Change screen brightness (DS / DS Lite only) L + Y Open settings L + X Open the cheat list for the selected game L + SELECT Temporarily show all files, not just games

The touch screen works too, you can tap on items, the START button and the folder-up button.

Tip

Can't remember all that? Press START and choose Help to see the main ones on screen.

docs.title: In game
docs.text: Once a game is running, the controls belong to the loader, not AKMenu-Next. With nds-bootstrap the default soft-reset combo is L + Down + SELECT, which takes you back to AKMenu-Next. You can change this with the Menu Hotkey setting (see Settings). The full list of nds-bootstrap controls is on the nds-bootstrap controls page.

docs.title: The start menu
docs.text:
Press START (or tap the button in the corner) to open it.

Option What it does Set favourite Add the selected file to Favourites Remove favourite Remove the selected file from Favourites File Info Same as pressing Y Themes Pick a different theme (see Themes) Tools Settings for an EZ-Flash 3-in-1 expansion pack, if you have one in Slot-2 Settings The main settings menu Help A quick list of controls About Your AKMenu-Next version, what mode it's running in, and which loaders it found

The About screen is really handy when something isn't working. It tells you if AKMenu-Next can actually see nds-bootstrap and Pico-Loader, and which versions they are.

docs.title: Favourites and Recently Played
docs.text:
Favourites is a shortcut list you build yourself. Highlight a game, press START and choose Set favourite. You can get to the list from the top level of the browser, or press X from anywhere.

Recently Played keeps track of the last 10 games you launched, newest first. Homebrew isn't added to it, but DS games, DSiWare and plugin files are.

docs.title: File list styles
docs.text:
Press SELECT to flip between the four styles, or set one permanently in Settings > Interface settings > Filelist style.

Style Looks like Old school Plain text list, no icons Modern Big icons with the file name Internal Big icons with the game's real title from its banner Small Icons Smaller icons so you can fit more on screen

If you'd like the list sorted by something other than file name, have a look at Sort by under File system settings. You can sort by game title or by date too.

docs.title: Launching games
docs.text:
Just highlight a game and press A. Here's what AKMenu-Next recognises out of the box:

Extension What it is Launched with .nds DS games and homebrew Your selected game loader (or homebrew loader for homebrew) .dsi, .srl, .ids DSi-enhanced / DSiWare / other DS ROM dumps Your selected game loader .ndz Compressed DS ROMs Always Pico-Loader .gba GBA ROMs EZ-Flash 3-in-1 if one is inserted, otherwise a gba plugin if you have one

Anything else needs a plugin, or you can press L + SELECT to see every file.

docs.title: Autorun
docs.text: If you turn on Autorun Last ROM (in Other Settings), AKMenu-Next will launch the last game you played straight away when it starts up. Hold B while AKMenu-Next is booting if you want to skip it and get to the menu.

docs.title: Per-game settings
docs.text:
Highlight a game, press Y to open its file info, then press Y again (the Settings button) to get its per-game settings. Anything set to default just follows the global setting from the main settings menu.

There are two tabs. Use L/R to switch between them.

Compatibility

Option What it does Select a save type Force a specific save size. Leave on unknown/auto unless a game isn't saving properly Game Loader Use Pico-Loader or nds-bootstrap for just this game (flashcart & DSpico only) nds-bootstrap version Release or nightly, for this game only DS-Only Mode Run this game in DS mode instead of DSi mode TWL CPU Speed Run this game at the DSi's faster CPU speed Card Read DMA Turn nds-bootstrap's card read DMA on or off for this game DSiWare booter Only shows up for DSiWare. Use nds-bootstrap or Unlaunch for this title

The nds-bootstrap options only show up when the game is actually going to use nds-bootstrap. If you change Game Loader to nds-bootstrap, save, then open the settings again and they'll appear.

Features

Option What it does Cheat in Game (AR) Enable or disable cheats for this game, or follow the global setting Choose Save Slot Which save slot to use (see save slots below) Show icon How the game's icon is drawn: transparent, as is, or how the DS firmware would show it

Per-game settings are stored in _nds/akmenunext/gamedata.bin, so if you ever want to wipe them all at once, delete that file.

docs.title: Saves
docs.text:
AKMenu-Next creates the save file for you the first time you launch a game, so there's nothing to set up. If there isn't enough free space on the card for the save, you'll get a "not enough space" error instead of the game booting.

Where the save goes depends on two settings in File system settings:

Use 'saves' folder Save extension Save for Games/Mario.nds ends up at Yes .sav Games/saves/Mario.sav Yes .nds.sav Games/saves/Mario.nds.sav No .sav Games/Mario.sav No .nds.sav Games/Mario.nds.sav

The Flashcart, DSi and 3DS editions use a saves folder by default. The DSpico edition puts saves next to the ROM by default.

Coming from another menu?

If your existing saves are somewhere else (for example, TWiLight Menu++ also uses a saves folder, but some kernels put .sav files next to the ROM), either move them to match, or change these two settings to match where your saves already are. Do this before launching the game, otherwise AKMenu-Next will make a fresh blank save.

docs.title: Save slots
docs.text:
Each game can have up to four separate saves. Slot "default" is the normal save file, and slots 1 to 3 add a number before the extension:

Mario.sav     <- default slot
Mario.1.sav   <- slot 1
Mario.2.sav   <- slot 2
Mario.3.sav   <- slot 3

Pick a slot from the game's per-game settings. Slots that already have a save file are marked with a *. There's also a global Save Slot Override in Other Settings which forces every game onto the same slot, handy if you're sharing the console with someone.

docs.title: DSiWare saves
docs.text: DSiWare uses .pub and .prv save files instead of .sav. These are made automatically too. See Running DSiWare for details.

docs.title: Cheats
docs.text:
1. Make sure you've got a usrcheat.dat in _nds/akmenunext/cheats/ (see the install guide for where to get one).

  2. Go to Settings > Other Settings and turn Cheat in Game(AR) on. This is the global switch.

  3. Highlight a game and press L + X, or press Y and then X (Cheats). You'll get the list of cheats for that game.

  4. In the cheat list:

    Button What it does A Tick or untick a cheat (or open a folder of cheats) Y Show the description for the selected cheat L Untick everything Left/Right Jump between cheat folders X Save your selection B Back out without saving

  5. Launch the game as normal. Your ticked cheats will be applied.

If you want cheats on for one game but off everywhere else, leave the global switch off and set Cheat in Game(AR) to on in that game's per-game settings.

Cheats work with both nds-bootstrap and Pico-Loader (make sure your Pico-Loader is up to date, older versions didn't support them). If the Cheats button doesn't show up in the file info window at all, AKMenu-Next can't find usrcheat.dat. If the button is there but nothing opens, that game probably just isn't in your cheat database.

Note

Cheats aren't available for homebrew. Some cheats in the database can crash games or corrupt saves, so if a game starts misbehaving, try it with cheats off.

docs.title: Slot-1 and Slot-2
docs.text:
• Slot 1 Card (DSi & 3DS SD card versions only) boots whatever game card is in the console's cartridge slot.
  • Slot 2 Card (DS & DS Lite) boots whatever's in the GBA slot. Depending on the Slot-2 mode setting it'll ask whether to start it in GBA mode or NDS mode, or just do one of them. If nothing is inserted you'll get a message saying so.

If you have an EZ-Flash 3-in-1 (or compatible) expansion pack inserted, .gba files on your SD card can be loaded into it. Press Y on a GBA ROM for the to NOR and to RAM buttons, and use Tools in the start menu for its rumble and memory settings. GBA ROMs bigger than 32MB aren't supported.
